summary_notes.cleaning: Masked NaN cadences, excluded cosmic ray anomalies via 5-sigma upper envelope clip.
summary_notes.detrending: Applied transit-preserving Savitzky-Golay running baseline filter (window = 3.5x duration).
summary_notes.folding: Folded by orbital period P = 37.4260 d around epoch T0 = 1326.495 BJD.
summary_notes.binning: Weighted Gaussian-kernel phase binning into 100 bins with empirical transit fit.

calculation_warnings: Single transit or limited cycle coverage; odd/even depth difference is unconstrained.

explanations.transit_depth_ppm: Fractional drop in stellar flux during transit (in parts per million). Genuine planets typically produce dips from 100 to 10,000 ppm; dips exceeding 20,000 ppm usually indicate an eclipsing binary star.
explanations.transit_duration_hours: Time elapsed between first and fourth contact (ingress to egress). Combined with orbital period, duration constrains the stellar density and orbital inclination.
explanations.signal_to_noise: Statistical significance of the transit signal relative to stellar and instrumental noise. SNR > 7.1 is the standard TESS threshold for a reliable transit detection.
explanations.odd_even_depth_diff_ppm: Difference in depth between consecutive transits. A significant depth difference is a definitive hallmark of an eclipsing binary with alternating primary and secondary stellar occultations.
explanations.secondary_eclipse_depth_ppm: Depth measured at phase 0.5 (anti-phase). Planets emit virtually no optical light compared to their stars, so a detectable secondary eclipse (>150 ppm) strongly indicates an eclipsing companion star.
explanations.in_transit_scatter: Residual scatter of photometric measurements inside the transit. High in-transit scatter can indicate stellar flare activity, starspot crossing, or blended background contaminants.

prediction_combined.astronomical_reasoning: The candidate was classified as Planet with 89.0% planet probability and 11.0% false-positive probability. Light-curve diagnostics show clean U-shaped profile, negligible odd/even depth variance, and no detectable secondary eclipse at phase 0.5.
scientific_limitations: This machine-learning classification is a diagnostic screening tool, not an official astronomical confirmation.
High stellar crowding or blended background stars within the 21-arcsecond TESS pixel aperture can mimic planetary transit depths.
Definitive planetary validation requires ground-based high-resolution imaging and high-precision radial velocity spectroscopy.
